docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Everything MT5Client from @metarpc/nodemt5 offers. Every call that the server answers with an error rejects with an MrpcError (err.code is the API's error code, e.g. TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND); a failed call (network, deadline) rejects with the gRPC error. Nothing is invented on failure.

docs.title: MT5Client
docs.text: Member new MT5Client(host = 'mt5.mrpc.pro', port = 443, apiKey?, id?) TLS on port 443, plaintext otherwise. apiKey defaults to MRPC_API_KEY, then TRIAL connect({ user, password, server }) ConnectEx by broker server name; connect({ user, password, host, port }) uses Connect by address; timeoutSeconds (default 60) connect(login, password, server = 'MetaQuotes-Demo') the same, short form getAccountInfo(): Promise<AccountInfo> see Account orderSend(request): Promise<OrderResult> see Trading subscribeQuotes(symbols, onQuote, onError?) OnSymbolTick stream; returns { unsubscribe() }, see Quotes disconnect(deleteTerminal = false) Disconnect; true also deletes the terminal. Closes the channel getId(login, password): Promise<string> GetId: the terminal id for these credentials MT5Client.openDemoAccount(server, apiKey, host = 'mt5.mrpc.pro') GET /DemoAccount/Open: a new demo account { login, password, server } client.id, client.connected the terminal id after connect(); whether connect() succeeded getGrpcMetadata() the apikey / id metadata, for your own calls through the generated clients

docs.title: Everything else
docs.text: The client covers connecting, the account, market orders and ticks. Every other method of the API (positions, history, symbol information, order modify/close, other streams) is in the generated gRPC clients the package exports (ConnectionGrpc, AccountHelperGrpc, TradingHelperGrpc, SubscriptionsGrpc, MarketInfoGrpc, ... with their *Pb messages) and under @metarpc/nodemt5/package/. Call them on the same host with client.getGrpcMetadata(); every reply has data or error. Every method, its request and reply: API methods; try them at https://mt5.mrpc.pro/apiui.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
const { MT5Client } = require('@metarpc/nodemt5');

const client = new MT5Client('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443, 'your-api-key');
await client.connect({ user: 5057401134, password: 'your-password', server: 'MetaQuotes-Demo' });
console.log('terminal', client.id);

// ... calls ...

await client.disconnect();        // or disconnect(true): stop the terminal and delete it

connect() resolves once the terminal is connected and rejects with an MrpcError when the server refuses (wrong password, unknown server, ...). To connect by address instead of broker server name, pass host and port instead of server.

There is no automatic reconnect in the client: if a call rejects with TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND or the channel fails, call connect() again.

docs.title: API key and terminal id
docs.text:
• APIKey: your key from https://mrpc.pro/my (sign up free at https://mrpc.pro/signup). Pass it to the constructor or set MRPC_API_KEY; without one the client sends TRIAL.
  • id: the terminal id. connect() receives it from the server (terminalInstanceGuid), keeps it in client.id and sends it with every later call and stream. You don't need to call getId() first.

docs.title: Quotes
docs.text:
const sub = client.subscribeQuotes(['EURUSD', 'GBPUSD'],
  (quote) => console.log(`${quote.symbol}: ${quote.bid} / ${quote.ask} at ${new Date(quote.time).toISOString()}`),
  (err) => console.error('stream error:', err.message));

// later
sub.unsubscribe();

quote.time is the tick time in milliseconds since the epoch (UTC). onError receives an error the stream answers with (for example NO_CHARTS_OPENED_FOR_SYMBOLS for a symbol the terminal doesn't have) or the stream's failure; an unsubscribe() is not an error. Bars and other market data are in the generated MarketInfoGrpc client.

docs.title: Trading
docs.text:
const order = await client.orderSend({ symbol: 'EURUSD', action: 'BUY', volume: 0.01, comment: 'first order' });
console.log(`Deal #${order.deal}, position #${order.order} at ${order.price} (return code ${order.retcode})`);
Request symbol, action (BUY, SELL, BUY_LIMIT, SELL_LIMIT, BUY_STOP, SELL_STOP), volume, optional price, stopLoss, takeProfit, slippage, comment Result retcode (10009 = done), deal, order (= ticket), volume, price, comment (the server's) An order the server refuses rejects with an MrpcError carrying the server's error code. Modifying and closing orders is done with the generated TradingHelperGrpc client (see API Reference).

docs.title: BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_FILLING
docs.text: Value Number Description BMT5_ORDER_FILLING_FOK 0 An order can be executed in the specified volume only. If the necessary amount of a financial instrument is currently unavailable in the market, the order will not be executed. The desired volume can be made up of several available offers. The possibility of using FOK orders is determined at the trade server. BMT5_ORDER_FILLING_IOC 1 A trader agrees to execute a deal with the volume maximally available in the market within that indicated in the order. If the request cannot be filled completely, an order with the available volume will be executed, and the remaining volume will be canceled. The possibility of using IOC orders is determined at the trade server. BMT5_ORDER_FILLING_BOC 3 The BoC order assumes that the order can only be placed in the Depth of Market and cannot be immediately executed. If the order can be executed immediately when placed, then it is canceled. In fact, the BOC policy guarantees that the price of the placed order will be worse than the current market. BoC orders are used to implement passive trading, so that the order is not executed immediately when placed and does not affect current liquidity. Only limit and stop limit orders are supported (ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT, ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT, ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT, ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT). BMT5_ORDER_FILLING_RETURN 2 In case of partial filling, an order with remaining volume is not canceled but processed further. Return orders are not allowed in the Market Execution mode (market execution — SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_MARKET).

docs.text: Value Number Description BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_FOREX 0 Forex mode - calculation of profit and margin for Forex // Margin: Lots * Contract_Size / Leverage * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * Contract_Size * Lots BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_FOREX_NO_LEVERAGE 1 Forex No Leverage mode – calculation of profit and margin for Forex symbols without taking into account the leverage // Margin: Lots * Contract_Size * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * Contract_Size * Lots BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_FUTURES 2 Futures mode - calculation of margin and profit for futures // Margin: Lots * InitialMargin * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * TickPrice / TickSize * Lots BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_CFD 3 CFD mode - calculation of margin and profit for CFD // Margin: Lots * ContractSize * MarketPrice * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * Contract_Size * Lots BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_CFDINDEX 4 CFD index mode - calculation of margin and profit for CFD by indexes // Margin: (Lots * ContractSize * MarketPrice) * TickPrice / TickSize * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * Contract_Size * Lots BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_CFDLEVERAGE 5 CFD Leverage mode - calculation of margin and profit for CFD at leverage trading // Margin: (Lots * ContractSize * MarketPrice) / Leverage * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * Contract_Size * Lots BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_EXCH_STOCKS 6 Exchange mode – calculation of margin and profit for trading securities on a stock exchange // Margin: Lots * ContractSize * LastPrice * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * Contract_Size * Lots BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_EXCH_FUTURES 7 Futures mode – calculation of margin and profit for trading futures contracts on a stock exchange // Margin: Lots * InitialMargin * Margin_Rate or Lots * MaintenanceMargin * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * Lots * TickPrice / TickSize BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_EXCH_FUTURES_FORTS 8 FORTS Futures mode – calculation of margin and profit for trading futures contracts on FORTS. The margin may be reduced by the amount of MarginDiscount deviation according to the following rules: // 1. If the price of a long position (buy order) is less than the estimated price, MarginDiscount = Lots * ((PriceSettle - PriceOrder) * TickPrice / TickSize) // 2. If the price of a short position (sell order) exceeds the estimated price, MarginDiscount = Lots * ((PriceOrder - PriceSettle) * TickPrice / TickSize) // where: // PriceSettle – estimated (clearing) price of the previous session; // PriceOrder – average weighted position price or open price set in the order (request); // TickPrice – tick price (cost of the price change by one point) // TickSize – tick size (minimum price change step) // Margin: Lots * InitialMargin * Margin_Rate or Lots * MaintenanceMargin * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * Lots * TickPrice / TickSize BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_EXCH_BONDS 9 Exchange Bonds mode – calculation of margin and profit for trading bonds on a stock exchange // Margin: Lots * ContractSize * FaceValue * open_price / 100 // Profit: Lots * close_price * FaceValue * Contract_Size + AccruedInterest * Lots * ContractSize BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_EXCH_STOCKS_MOEX 10 Exchange MOEX Stocks mode – calculation of margin and profit for trading securities on MOEX // Margin: Lots * ContractSize * LastPrice * Margin_Rate // Profit: (close_price - open_price) * Contract_Size * Lots BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_EXCH_BONDS_MOEX 11 Exchange MOEX Bonds mode – calculation of margin and profit for trading bonds on MOEX // Margin: Lots * ContractSize * FaceValue * open_price / 100 // Profit: Lots * close_price * FaceValue * Contract_Size + AccruedInterest * Lots * ContractSize BMT5_SYMBOL_CALC_MODE_SERV_COLLATERAL 12 Collateral mode - a symbol is used as a non-tradable asset on a trading account. The market value of an open position is calculated based on the volume, current market price, contract size and liquidity ratio. The value is included into Assets, which are added to Equity. Open positions of such symbols increase the Free Margin amount and are used as additional margin (collateral) for open positions of tradable instruments. // Margin: no // Profit: no // Market Value: Lots * ContractSize * MarketPrice * LiquidityRate

docs.title: MRPC_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_FILLING
docs.text: Value Number Description ORDER_FILLING_FOK 0 An order can be executed in the specified volume only. If the necessary amount of a financial instrument is currently unavailable in the market, the order will not be executed. The desired volume can be made up of several available offers. The possibility of using FOK orders is determined at the trade server. ORDER_FILLING_IOC 1 A trader agrees to execute a deal with the volume maximally available in the market within that indicated in the order. If the request cannot be filled completely, an order with the available volume will be executed, and the remaining volume will be canceled. The possibility of using IOC orders is determined at the trade server. ORDER_FILLING_BOC 3 The BoC order assumes that the order can only be placed in the Depth of Market and cannot be immediately executed. If the order can be executed immediately when placed, then it is canceled. In fact, the BOC policy guarantees that the price of the placed order will be worse than the current market. BoC orders are used to implement passive trading, so that the order is not executed immediately when placed and does not affect current liquidity. Only limit and stop limit orders are supported (ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT, ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT, ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT, ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT). ORDER_FILLING_RETURN 2 In case of partial filling, an order with remaining volume is not canceled but processed further. Return orders are not allowed in the Market Execution mode (market execution — SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_MARKET).

docs.title: SUB_ENUM_TRADE_TRANSACTION_TYPE
docs.text: Value Number Description SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_ORDER_ADD 0 Adding a new open order. SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_ORDER_UPDATE 1 Updating an open order. The updates include not only evident changes from the client terminal or a trade server sides but also changes of an order state when setting it (for example, transition from ORDER_STATE_STARTED to ORDER_STATE_PLACED or from ORDER_STATE_PLACED to ORDER_STATE_PARTIAL, etc.). SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_ORDER_DELETE 2 Removing an order from the list of the open ones. An order can be deleted from the open ones as a result of setting an appropriate request or execution (filling) and moving to the history. SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_DEAL_ADD 3 Adding a deal to the history. The action is performed as a result of an order execution or performing operations with an account balance. SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_DEAL_UPDATE 4 Updating a deal in the history. There may be cases when a previously executed deal is changed on a server. For example, a deal has been changed in an external trading system (exchange) where it was previously transferred by a broker. SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_DEAL_DELETE 5 Deleting a deal from the history. There may be cases when a previously executed deal is deleted from a server. For example, a deal has been deleted in an external trading system (exchange) where it was previously transferred by a broker. SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_HISTORY_ADD 6 Adding an order to the history as a result of execution or cancellation. SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_HISTORY_UPDATE 7 Changing an order located in the orders history. This type is provided for enhancing functionality on a trade server side. SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_HISTORY_DELETE 8 Deleting an order from the orders history. This type is provided for enhancing functionality on a trade server side. SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_POSITION 9 Changing a position not related to a deal execution. This type of transaction shows that a position has been changed on a trade server side. Position volume, open price, Stop Loss and Take Profit levels can be changed. Data on changes are submitted in MqlTradeTransaction structure via OnTradeTransaction handler. Position change (adding, changing or closing), as a result of a deal execution, does not lead to the occurrence of TRADE_TRANSACTION_POSITION transaction. SUB_TRADE_TRANSACTION_REQUEST 10 Notification of the fact that a trade request has been processed by a server and processing result has been received. Only type field (trade transaction type) must be analyzed for such transactions in MqlTradeTransaction structure. The second and third parameters of OnTradeTransaction (request and result) must be analyzed for additional data.

docs.title: API methods
docs.text: Every public method of the MT5 API, generated from the protos this package is built from. Each is a gRPC method of package mt5_term_api on mt5.mrpc.pro:443 and a REST route on https://mt5.mrpc.pro (server streams also as a WebSocket on the same path, wss://mt5.mrpc.pro/...?id=...&apikey=...). Every reply carries either data (described below) or error (see Errors). Try them in the browser: https://mt5.mrpc.pro/apiui.

docs.title: Calling a method
docs.text:
Every method below is a method of the generated client of its service ({Service}Grpc / {Service}Pb from @metarpc/nodemt5). Call it on the client's host with client.getGrpcMetadata() (the API key and the terminal id):

const { MT5Client, MarketInfoGrpc, MarketInfoPb } = require('@metarpc/nodemt5');
const grpc = require('@grpc/grpc-js');

const marketInfo = new MarketInfoGrpc.MarketInfoClient('mt5.mrpc.pro:443', grpc.credentials.createSsl());
const request = new MarketInfoPb.QuoteRequest();
request.setSymbol('EURUSD');
marketInfo.quote(request, client.getGrpcMetadata(), (err, reply) => {
  if (err) throw err;                                   // the call failed
  if (reply.getError()) throw new Error(reply.getError().getErrorMessage());   // the API answered with an error
  console.log(reply.getData().getBid(), reply.getData().getAsk());
});

Field foo_bar is getFooBar() / setFooBar(value); a repeated field is getFooBarList() / setFooBarList([...]); an enum value is XxxPb.EnumName.VALUE. A server stream is client.method(request, metadata) with on('data' | 'error' | 'end').

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text: ============================================================================ Accounts: the MT5 accounts (terminals) that belong to your API key. This is the call to make when you need the terminal ids of accounts that already exist - started from the dashboard or by an earlier ConnectEx - so that you can send them as the "id" header of every other call. Unlike the terminal calls it needs NO "id" header: it is answered from the platform's records of the API key sent in the "APIKey" header, and it never starts, wakes or bills a terminal. Accounts are listed newest first (by started_utc, then terminal_id) and returned by page. Only accounts of THIS platform's endpoint are listed (mt5.mrpc.pro lists MT5 accounts, mt4.mrpc.pro lists MT4 accounts). ============================================================================

docs.title: Accounts.List
docs.text:
Lists the accounts of the API key sent in the APIKey header, one page per call. Pass the next_page_token of a page back as page_token to continue; an empty next_page_token means that was the last page. [DefaultValues] { "includeStopped": "false", "pageSize": "200" }

  • gRPC: mt5_term_api.Accounts/List (unary)
  • REST: GET /Accounts

Request AccountsListRequest

Field Node Type Description state getState() string Only accounts in this state, e.g. "Connected", "Syncing", "Unreachable", "WrongPassword", "Suspended" (the vocabulary of ConnectState.state, compared without regard to case). Empty = every state. login getLogin() uint64 Only the account with this login number. 0 = every login. include_stopped getIncludeStopped() bool false (default): only accounts that are queued, starting or running, or that stopped on their own (Unreachable, WrongPassword, Suspended, Expired) and can be started again. true: also accounts that were stopped by the user, by an API call or by an administrator. Deleted accounts are never listed. page_size getPageSize() int32 Accounts per page, 1..1000. 0 = 200. A larger value is clamped, a negative one is rejected with ACCOUNTS_PAGE_SIZE_INVALID. page_token getPageToken() string The next_page_token of the previous page; empty for the first page. Must be sent with the same state, login and include_stopped. Undecodable -> ACCOUNTS_PAGE_TOKEN_INVALID.

Reply data AccountsListData

Leave both at 0 to take the newest max_bars bars instead, which is what a chart opening on a symbol actually wants. from_time_utc getFromTimeUtc() int64 from_time in UTC: send either from_time or from_time_utc, not both. to_time getToTime() int64 to_time_utc getToTimeUtc() int64 to_time in UTC: send either to_time or to_time_utc, not both. max_bars getMaxBars() int32 Upper bound on the answer. docs.title: QuoteHistory
docs.text: ============================================================================ Quote history: the bars a chart is drawn from, and the ticks those bars are built from, for one symbol - returned by PAGE, oldest first. Both calls walk a time range forward. A page carries at most page_size items and, when the range holds more, a next_page_token; passing that token back (same symbol, timeframe/flags and range) returns the next page. An empty next_page_token means the range is exhausted. Tokens are opaque: a client stores and returns them, nothing else. History lives in the terminal and is fetched from the broker on demand. The first request for a symbol or a period the terminal has not loaded yet can take a few seconds, and when the broker has not delivered it within that time the call answers with an error whose error_code is QUOTE_HISTORY_NOT_READY - ask again a moment later. Nothing is served from a cache outside the terminal. Every call needs the terminal id header ("id"), like every other call. ============================================================================

docs.title: QuoteHistory.Bars
docs.text:
OHLC bars (candles) of one symbol and timeframe, oldest first, by page.

  • gRPC: mt5_term_api.QuoteHistory/Bars (unary)
  • REST: GET /QuoteHistory/Bars

Request QuoteHistoryBarsRequest

Field Node Type Description symbol getSymbol() string Required. Broker symbol name, e.g. "EURUSD". timeframe getTimeframe() QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME Required. from_time getFromTime() int64 Required. Unix seconds (UTC) of the oldest bar wanted, inclusive. A time before the broker's first bar is clamped to that first bar. from_time_utc getFromTimeUtc() int64 from_time in UTC: send either from_time or from_time_utc, not both. to_time getToTime() int64 Unix seconds (UTC) of the newest bar wanted, inclusive. 0 = now. to_time_utc getToTimeUtc() int64 to_time in UTC: send either to_time or to_time_utc, not both. page_size getPageSize() int32 Bars per page, 1..5000. 0 = 1000. page_token getPageToken() string The next_page_token of the previous page, to continue; empty for the first page. Must be used with the same symbol, timeframe and range.

Reply data QuoteHistoryBarsData

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every reply of the API carries either data or error; a refused request is an answer like any other (HTTP 200 on REST), not a failed call.

Every call of MT5Client resolves with what the server answered or rejects:

  • with an MrpcError when the API answered with an error: err.code is the error code, err.message the code and message, err.error the reply's whole Error (the fields below);
  • with the gRPC error when the call failed (network, deadline, server down): err.code is the gRPC status number (grpc.status.UNAVAILABLE, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, ...).

With the generated clients you get the reply itself: reply.getError() is set instead of reply.getData().

docs.title: A refused order
docs.text:
const { MrpcError } = require('@metarpc/nodemt5');

try {
  await client.orderSend({ symbol: 'EURUSD', action: 'BUY', volume: 0.001 });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof MrpcError && err.error) {                  // the API answered with an error
    console.log(err.code);                                    // MQL5_SIDE_TRADE_ERROR
    console.log(err.error.getMqlErrorTradeIntCode());         // 10014 (TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_VOLUME)
    console.log(err.error.getMqlErrorTradeDescription());     // Invalid volume in the request
  } else {
    throw err;                                                // the call failed: err.code is the gRPC status
  }
}

When the broker or the terminal refuses a trade request, the trade server's return code is in mql_error_trade_int_code / mql_error_trade_code (MqlErrorTradeCode: 10014 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_VOLUME, 10019 TRADE_RETCODE_NO_MONEY, ...), the error type is MQL_TRADE_EXECUTION and error_code is MQL5_SIDE_TRADE_ERROR.

docs.title: The error
docs.text:
Error has:

Field error_code what went wrong, e.g. TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND; use it in your code error_message the same for people, with details type where it happened (ErrorType): MRPC, MRPC_VALIDATION, MRPC_TIMEOUT, MQL_EXECUTION, ... mql_error_code, mql_error_int_code, mql_error_description the MQL error of the terminal, when the terminal refused (MqlErrorCode) mql_error_trade_code, mql_error_trade_int_code, mql_error_trade_description the trade server's return code of a refused order command_type_name the terminal command that failed

docs.title: Codes you will meet
docs.text:
error_code Meaning What to do TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND the terminal id is not a running terminal (never was, or stopped) connect again MQL5_SIDE_TRADE_ERROR the terminal refused the request: see the MQL fields fix the request (volume, price, stops, ...) NO_CHARTS_OPENED_FOR_SYMBOLS a tick stream for symbols the terminal does not have check the symbol names

The codes of the limits (calls per minute, the order queue, tick streams) and of the API key: Errors & Limits.

docs.title: Getting Started with NodeMT5
docs.text: Quick Setup & Overview - Connect to MetaTrader 5 from Node.js in a few minutes.

docs.title: What is NodeMT5?
docs.text:
NodeMT5 is a Node.js and TypeScript client for MetaTrader 5 accounts through the MRPC gRPC API (mt5.mrpc.pro:443). It has two parts:

  • MT5Client: connect, account, market orders, tick stream, disconnect (see API Reference).
  • The generated gRPC clients of the whole API (ConnectionGrpc, AccountHelperGrpc, TradingHelperGrpc, SubscriptionsGrpc, MarketInfoGrpc, ...), exported by the package, for everything else.

The other pages of these guides describe the API itself (methods, enums, return codes, streams); some of their code samples are in Python, the calls and messages are the same from Node.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: npm install github:MetaRPC/NodeMT5 @grpc/grpc-js

docs.title: The package is installed from GitHub; it is not on the npm registry. It is named @metarpc/nodemt5, so require('@metarpc/nodemt5') works as usual.
API key
docs.text:
1. Sign up free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Create a key at https://mrpc.pro/my under API Keys.
  3. Pass it to new MT5Client(host, 443, apiKey) or set MRPC_API_KEY.

docs.title: API key and terminal id
docs.text:
• APIKey: your key from https://mrpc.pro/my (sign up free at https://mrpc.pro/signup). Pass it to the constructor or set MRPC_API_KEY; without one the client sends TRIAL.
  • id: the terminal id. connect() receives it from the server (terminalInstanceGuid), keeps it in client.id and sends it with every later call and stream. You don't need to call getId() first.

docs.title:
const { MT5Client } = require('@metarpc/nodemt5');

async function main() {
  const client = new MT5Client('mt5.mrpc.pro', 443, process.env.MRPC_API_KEY);
  await client.connect({ user: Number(process.env.MT5_LOGIN), password: process.env.MT5_PASSWORD, server: 'MetaQuotes-Demo' });
  try {
    const account = await client.getAccountInfo();
    console.log(`Balance: ${account.balance} ${account.currency}, equity ${account.equity}, leverage 1:${account.leverage}`);

    const order = await client.orderSend({ symbol: 'EURUSD', action: 'BUY', volume: 0.01, comment: 'first order' });
    console.log(`Deal #${order.deal}, position #${order.order} at ${order.price} (return code ${order.retcode})`);
  } finally {
    await client.disconnect();
  }
}

main().catch((err) => { console.error(err.message); process.exit(1); });

docs.title: Streams
docs.text:
The API pushes data over gRPC server streams. Ticks have their own method in the client: client.subscribeQuotes(symbols, onQuote, onError). Every other stream is a method of SubscriptionServiceGrpc:

Stream What it sends OnSymbolTick ticks of the symbols OnTrade every change of orders, positions and deals, with the account values OnPositionProfit the profit of the open positions and the account values, every timer_period_milliseconds OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets the tickets of open positions and pending orders, every timer_period_milliseconds OnTradeTransaction the trade transactions of the terminal (MQL5 OnTradeTransaction) OnConnectState the state of your terminals (Connected, Unreachable, Stopped, ...) OnJournal, OnExperts the terminal's journal and Experts log (a new stream starts with what is already written)

Their requests and messages: API methods.

docs.title: Using a stream
docs.text:
OnPositionProfit, the account's equity, margin and profit every second:

const grpc = require('@grpc/grpc-js');
const { MT5Client, SubscriptionsPb } = require('@metarpc/nodemt5');

// client: a connected MT5Client
const request = new SubscriptionsPb.OnPositionProfitRequest();
request.setTimerPeriodMilliseconds(1000);
const stream = client.subscriptionClient.onPositionProfit(request, client.getGrpcMetadata());

stream.on('data', (reply) => {
  if (reply.getError()) {                                     // the API answered with an error
    console.error('stream error:', reply.getError().getErrorCode(), reply.getError().getErrorMessage());
    return;
  }
  const data = reply.getData();
  if (!data) return;                                          // a heartbeat (after 30 s without data)
  const account = data.getAccountInfo();
  console.log(`equity ${account.getEquity()}, margin ${account.getMargin()}, profit ${account.getProfit()}`);
});
stream.on('error', (err) => {
  if (err.code === grpc.status.CANCELLED) return;             // stream.cancel()
  console.error('stream failed:', err.message);               // open it again
});

// ... when done
stream.cancel();
  • Every message has data or error. A message with neither is a heartbeat: after 30 seconds without data the server sends one so that proxies keep the connection open. Skip it.
  • An error message reports a problem with the stream's request (for example NO_CHARTS_OPENED_FOR_SYMBOLS for a symbol the terminal does not have); the stream may end after it.
  • stream.cancel() ends it (the error event then has code CANCELLED, which is not a failure).
  • A stream does not resume by itself. When it fails or ends while you still need it, open it again; when calls answer TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, the terminal is gone: connect first.
  • Opening a stream counts as a call toward the per-terminal limits, the messages it delivers do not; the number of tick streams per terminal is limited too: Errors & Limits.

docs.title: In a browser
docs.text: Browsers cannot speak gRPC to the API (no gRPC-Web is served). Every stream is also a WebSocket on its REST path, with the terminal id and key in the query: wss://mt5.mrpc.pro/OnPositionProfit?id=<terminal id>&apikey=<key>&timerPeriodMilliseconds=1000. See the client guide.
